feature_summary:
- The Jeep Meridian is a premium, feature-rich SUV from Jeep India that blends bold SUV design, robust performance, advanced safety technology, a refined interior, and modern connectivity. The official ex-showroom price range starts from ₹23.33 lakh - rest assured that you will get the best deal at the dealership. It stands out with a strong 2.0 L Multijet II diesel engine paired with a 9-speed automatic or 6-speed manual, capable performance in both 4x2 and 4x4 configurations, and legendary Jeep capability. The exterior combines a powerful stance with signature Jeep design cues, LED headlamps, muscular body lines and 18-inch alloy wheels that convey both presence and capability. Inside, Meridian offers a premium cabin with spacious seating in 5-seater and 7-seater options, 12-way powered front seats, dual-zone automatic climate control, leather/vegan leather upholstery, and flexible boot space. The SUV’s infotainment is anchored by a large Uconnect touchscreen (10.1-inch) with wireless Apple CarPlay/Android Auto, integrated navigation, connected car features including Alexa Home-to-Vehicle support, remote engine start/stop with AC pre-conditioning and smartwatch connectivity, making it tech-forward and intuitive. Meridian also emphasises entertainment with a quality audio system and immersive digital displays. On the safety front, it comes standard with six airbags, ABS with EBD, traction control, electronic stability control, hill start assist, electronic parking brake, tyre pressure monitoring system, 360° cameras and a comprehensive ADAS suite (Adaptive Cruise Control, Forward Collision Mitigation Braking, Lane Keep Assist, Blind Spot Detection, Intelligent Speed Assist and more) on top trims, delivering high confidence and protection. 
 - The variant lineup for Jeep Meridian as per the official Jeep India site and updated market guides includes Longitude, Longitude Plus, Limited (O), and Overland, each catering to different customer needs and budget brackets with official ex-showroom pricing starting around ₹23.33 Lakh* for the base Meridian Longitude and rising to the top-spec Overland 4×4 AT. The Longitude variant offers essential SUV highlights like LED headlights with DRLs, roof rails, dual-zone climate control, a semi-digital instrument cluster, 10.1-inch infotainment with wireless smartphone connectivity, basic safety suite and cruise control, making it a strong value proposition. The Longitude Plus builds on this by adding a panoramic sunroof, contrast roof, wireless charger, leather steering wheel, auto-dimming IRVM, and third-row reclining seats for greater comfort and convenience. The Limited (O) variant steps up the luxury and technology with features like powered 8-way driver and front passenger seats with memory, ventilated seats, a larger digital instrument cluster, a premium Alpine 9-speaker sound system, third-row AC vents, a powered tailgate and a 360° camera, enhancing the Meridian’s upscale appeal. The Overland is the top-tier offering that adds chrome accents, suede interior touches, 4×4 capability with Jeep Active Drive and Selec-Terrain, and a comprehensive Level-2 ADAS suite (including adaptive cruise, lane departure warnings, collision mitigation and more) for the most advanced safety and off-road confidence. Additionally, Jeep has introduced special editions like Meridian X and Meridian Upland that bring unique styling and accessory enhancements for lifestyle and adventurous buyers.
 - The Meridian’s colour palette includes a variety of premium exterior shades such as Techno Metallic Green, Brilliant Black, Pearl White, Velvet Red, Magnesio Grey, Galaxy Blue, Silvery Moon and Minimal Grey, allowing buyers to personalise their SUV’s presence. 
 - When compared with competitors such as the Toyota Fortuner, MG Gloster, and Skoda Kodiaq, the Jeep Meridian offers several compelling advantages. Against the Toyota Fortuner, Meridian generally comes at a lower entry price while still delivering sophisticated interior technology, advanced connectivity and modern ADAS capabilities that are optional or less comprehensive on the Fortuner, making Meridian a strong choice for tech-centric buyers seeking a premium SUV experience. Versus the MG Gloster, while both offer ADAS and premium features, Meridian combines legendary Jeep off-road credibility with a more engaging driving feel and connected tech (Alexa integration, remote pre-conditioning) that gives it an edge in usability and lifestyle integration. In comparison to the Skoda Kodiaq, Meridian typically offers better value with its competitive feature set and 4×4 capability options at a similar price point, along with Jeep’s rugged brand heritage appealing to customers valuing both urban luxury and trail capability. Overall, the Jeep Meridian stands out for its blend of advanced safety technology, robust performance, premium interior comfort, and modern connectivity features, positioning it as a compelling choice in the premium SUV segment.

feature_summary:
- The Citroen Basalt X is India’s first SUV-Coupe in its segment, combining bold French styling with comfort-led engineering and certified safety to deliver a distinctive yet practical driving experience. an official ex-showroom price range starts from ₹8.14 lakh - rest assured that you will get the best deal at the dealership.  Built around Citroen’s global comfort DNA, it merges SUV versatility with a sporty coupe silhouette, offering strong road presence alongside everyday usability. The Basalt X has earned a 4-Star Safety Rating from Bharat NCAP for both Adult and Child Occupant Protection, confirming its strong structural integrity and crash performance under official testing standards. Supporting this rating, it comes equipped with comprehensive passive safety features including 6 airbags (driver, passenger, side and curtain), 3-point seatbelts for all occupants, seatbelt reminders for every seat, and ISOFIX child seat anchors with top tether, ensuring protection across the cabin. Active safety systems such as ESP (Electronic Stability Program), Hill Hold Assist, and ABS with EBD enhance stability, maintain grip during sudden manoeuvres, prevent skidding, and avoid rollback on inclines, helping prevent accidents before they occur. Visibility and driver awareness are strengthened with the Halo 360° Camera, reverse parking sensors, auto-dimming IRVM, LED Vision projector headlamps, projector fog lamps, and signature LED DRLs, providing confidence in tight city spaces and low-light conditions. The vehicle also proactively safeguards occupants through features like the Tyre Pressure Monitoring System and High Speed Alert system, which issues warnings at 80 km/h and continuous alerts at 120 km/h, ensuring risks are identified early. 
 - Beyond safety, the Basalt X offers a connected ecosystem with remote AC pre-conditioning, remote lock/unlock, live vehicle diagnostics, and full integration with the MyCitroen app. Inside, the technology experience is anchored by a 10.25-inch lag-free touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, wireless charging, and a 7-inch digital driver display, delivering seamless connectivity. A key highlight in higher variants is CARA, India’s first intelligent in-car companion in the segment, designed to go beyond basic voice commands by enabling continuous, contextual conversation. CARA personalizes interactions by remembering user preferences, supports navigation, weather updates, flight status checks, and real-time information access, enables calling and SOS assistance, controls multimedia functions, and even provides vehicle-related guidance. With multilingual capability and natural speech recognition, CARA transforms the cabin into an interactive and intelligent environment. Together, certified crash safety, active stability systems, preventive alerts, connected technology, and AI-powered assistance position the Citroen Basalt X as a stylish, secure, and smart SUV-coupe built for modern drivers. 
 - Regarding variants and their unique highlights, Basalt is offered in three core trims: You, Plus and Max, with multiple variant permutations including NA and Turbo petrol options, and manual/automatic gearboxes. The entry-level 'You' focuses on essentials with halogen headlamps, steel wheels, basic safety suite (6 airbags, ABS, ESP, HHC, ISOFIX), manual AC and reverse parking sensors — delivering strong value at the base price. The 'Plus' variant adds a more upscale experience with LED DRLs, wheel covers, body-coloured handles, ORVM turn indicators, interior dual-tone trim, a larger touchscreen, digital driver display, height-adjustable driver seat and TPMS, elevating both comfort and tech. With the turbo engine in Plus, you get projector headlamps, fog lamps, automatic climate control, rear AC vents, rear defogger, and dual USB chargers — making it a compelling mid-range pick. The top-end 'Max' garners 16-inch alloy wheels, leather-wrapped steering wheel, semi-leatherette seats, connected car features, shark-fin antenna, rear camera, and smart tilt rear cushion (in AT) with dual-tone roof options that accentuate premium appeal. 
 -In terms of colours available for Basalt, buyers can choose from single-tone shades including Polar White, Steel Grey, Platinum Grey, Cosmo Blue, and Garnet Red, along with dual-tone combinations like Polar White with Black roof and Garnet Red with Black roof, offering both classic and contrasting looks.
 - When compared with key competitors such as the Hyundai Creta, Kia Seltos and Tata Curvv, the Basalt holds its own due to its distinctive SUV-coupe styling and comfort-focused ride quality that’s often cited as more compliance-oriented than the typically firmer rivals. Against the Creta and Seltos, which are more mainstream SUVs with broader feature lists and dealer networks, Basalt delivers a unique exterior character with competitive safety and infotainment tech at a generally lower entry price, appealing to buyers seeking standout design and value — especially with features like a large touchscreen, connected car tech and advanced comfort suspension. Versus the Tata Curvv, Basalt’s ride comfort and brand-exclusive suspension tuning can be a preference point for buyers focused on long-journey ease and a more European ride feel, whereas Curvv leans more toward performance-oriented dynamics. In each comparison, Basalt’s combination of bold design, solid safety equipment, comfort-centric features and competitive pricing make it a compelling alternative to these established rivals for customers prioritising style and comfort without spending significantly more.

feature_summary:
- The Citroen Aircross X is a bold and versatile SUV designed for modern Indian families, combining French design sophistication with SUV strength and everyday practicality. The official ex-showroom price starts from ₹8.29 lakh for the 5-Seater and ₹10.99 lakh for the 7-Seater - rest assured that you will get the best deal at the dealership. Built around Citroen's global comfort DNA and engineered in India, the Aircross X offers commanding road presence with 200 mm ground clearance, a muscular stance, and distinctive diamond-cut alloy wheels that enhance its strong SUV identity. Designed for flexibility, the Aircross X is available in both 5-seater and 7-seater configurations, with the 7-seater featuring Flexi-Pro seating, removable third-row seats, 60:40 split second-row tumble function, and a 3-step recline feature for maximum adaptability between passengers and luggage. Comfort remains central to the Aircross X experience with Citroen's signature suspension tuning that delivers a smooth and planted ride across varying road conditions. Best-in-class tropicalised automatic climate control, rear AC vents, rear roof vents (7-seater), and Tropicool ventilated front seats ensure superior cabin comfort even during peak Indian summers. The lounge-inspired interior features soft-touch materials, leatherette upholstery in higher trims, diffused ambient lighting, and a refined dual-tone cabin theme that creates a premium and relaxed driving environment. On the technology front, the Aircross X comes equipped with a 10.25-inch Citroen Connect floating touchscreen with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, paired with a 7-inch coloured digital TFT instrument cluster. Wireless charging, multiple Type-C fast charging ports across rows, cruise control with speed limiter, and Proxi-Sense passive entry with push start enhance convenience and everyday usability. A key highlight in higher variants is CARA, India's intelligent in-car companion, designed to go beyond basic voice commands with continuous conversations, personalised interactions, navigation assistance, weather updates, multimedia control, SOS support, and real-time information access with multilingual capability, transforming the cabin into a smart and interactive ecosystem. The Aircross X also integrates 40+ connected features through the MyCitroen Connect app including remote engine start/stop with pre-conditioning, geo-fencing, remote lock/unlock, intrusion alerts, fuel status monitoring, and vehicle tracking. The Aircross has a 5-star Bharat NCAP rating for Adult Occupant Protection and 4 stars for Child Occupant Protection. Safety is comprehensive with 6 airbags, Electronic Stability Program (ESP), Hill Hold Assist, ABS with EBD, ISOFIX child seat anchors with top tether, Tyre Pressure Monitoring System (TPMS), reverse parking sensors, electrochromic auto-dimming IRVM, and an available 360° camera system, along with high-speed alert warnings at 80 km/h and continuous alerts at 120 km/h to enhance preventive safety. Under the hood, the Aircross X offers PureTech petrol powertrains including a 1.2L naturally aspirated engine and a 1.2L turbo petrol engine with 5-speed manual, 6-speed manual, and 6-speed torque converter automatic transmission options, delivering strong mid-range performance with competitive fuel efficiency. 
 - Regarding variants and their unique highlights, Aircross X is offered in three core trims: You, Plus, and Max across both 5-seater and 7-seater configurations with NA and Turbo petrol options. The entry-level 'You' 5-Seater starts at ₹8.29 lakh  and focuses on essentials with 6 airbags, ABS, ESP, Hill Hold Assist, manual AC, reverse parking sensors, and core comfort features, delivering strong value at the base price. The 7-Seater range starts from ₹10.99 lakh  and adds flexible third-row seating with enhanced practicality for larger families. The 'Plus' variant enhances the experience with a larger touchscreen, digital cluster, automatic climate control (with turbo), rear AC vents, additional charging ports, cruise control in select variants, and improved interior trims, offering a balanced mix of comfort and technology. The top-end 'Max' variant adds 17-inch diamond-cut alloy wheels, leatherette upholstery, ambient lighting, wireless charger, electrochromic IRVM, connected car features with 40+ smart functions, CARA intelligent assistant (in automatic variant), Proxi-Sense passive entry with push start, and dual-tone roof options, delivering a premium and tech-forward experience. 
 - In terms of colours available for Aircross X, buyers can choose from monotone shades including Polar White, Steel Grey, Deep Forest Green, Cosmo Blue, Garnet Red, and Perla Nera Black, along with dual-tone combinations like Polar White with Black roof, Deep Forest Green with Black roof, Cosmo Blue with Polar White roof, and Garnet Red with Black roof, offering both elegant and sporty styling choices. 
 - When compared with key competitors such as Hyundai Creta, Kia Seltos and Tata Curvv, the Aircross X stands out with its flexible 5 and 7-seater configuration, removable third-row seats, comfort-focused suspension tuning, and intelligent in-car assistant technology. While rivals may emphasize feature density or performance orientation, Aircross X prioritizes ride comfort, cabin flexibility, connected convenience, and family-centric usability, making it a compelling alternative for buyers seeking space, practicality, and distinctive European-inspired design at a competitive starting price.

 - The R15S is the ideal choice for solo sport riders who prioritise MotoGP-inspired aesthetics, Yamaha brand value and a focussed track-day visual character over everyday pillion carrying practicality, backed by the proven liquid-cooled VVA Deltabox platform.
competitor_vehicles: KTM RC 200, Honda CBR150R, Bajaj Pulsar RS200

major_changes: New bodywork inspired by R1, slipper clutch, assist clutch
feature_summary:
The Yamaha YZF-R3 is a middleweight fully-faired sports motorcycle powered by a 321cc liquid-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke parallel twin-cylinder DOHC engine producing 42 PS at 10,750 rpm and 29.5 Nm at 9,000 rpm, paired with a 6-speed gearbox with assist and slipper clutch, delivering a genuinely thrilling high-revving twin-cylinder sports experience at an accessible price point. 
 - The chassis is a steel Deltabox frame with 41 mm telescopic front forks, a preload adjustable mono-shock rear suspension, 298 mm front dual disc brakes and a 220 mm rear disc with dual-channel ABS, 17-inch alloy wheels with 110/70 front and 150/60 rear radial tyres giving it excellent stability and cornering confidence at speed. 
 - The full aerodynamic fairing with twin LED headlamps, DRLs, a large aerodynamic screen and MotoGP-inspired livery options make the R3 visually one of the most dramatic motorcycles in its class, directly inspired by the YZF-R1 race machine and used in the Yamaha R3 Cup one-make racing series. 
 - The fully digital instrument console shows speed, RPM, fuel gauge, gear indicator, lap timer, tripmeter and clock, while sport-focused clip-on handlebars and rear-set footpegs create an aggressive tuck position for maximum rider and motorcycle aerodynamic efficiency at speed. 
 - Available in Matte Black, Racing Blue and Icon Performance liveries with a 14-litre fuel tank and approximately 26 to 30 kmpl claimed fuel efficiency, the R3 is priced at approximately Rs 4.65 lakh to Rs 4.85 lakh ex-showroom competing with KTM RC 390, BMW G310RR and Kawasaki Ninja 300.

competitor_vehicles: KTM RC 390, Honda CBR300R, Kawasaki Ninja 400

remarks: Naked street fighter based on R3 platform
feature_summary:
The Yamaha MT-03 is a naked street fighter derivative of the YZF-R3, sharing the same 321cc liquid-cooled parallel twin-cylinder DOHC engine producing 42 PS at 10,750 rpm and 29.5 Nm at 9,000 rpm, paired with a 6-speed gearbox with assist and slipper clutch, but wrapped in Yamaha's iconic MT series aggressive naked styling inspired by the larger MT-07 and MT-09. 
 - The chassis is identical to the R3 with a steel Deltabox frame, 41 mm telescopic forks, preload adjustable mono-shock rear, 298 mm front dual discs, 220 mm rear disc and dual-channel ABS, 17-inch alloy wheels with 110/70 front and 150/60 rear radial tyres, but the MT-03 swaps the full fairing for minimalist bodywork delivering a dramatically different, aggressive streetfighter personality. 
 - The signature round hexagonal LED headlamp unit with DRLs is a hallmark of the MT series design language, while the muscular fuel tank, minimal tail section and wide handlebar give the MT-03 an upright, confident and intimidating naked roadster stance distinctly unlike any other motorcycle at this price point. 
 - The fully digital instrument console offers speed, tachometer, fuel gauge, gear indicator, tripmeter and clock, while the more upright ergonomics with wide handlebars and slightly rear-set footpegs strike a comfortable balance between relaxed street riding and sport-inspired dynamic control. 
 - Available in Metallic Black, Cyan Storm and Ice Fluo-Vermillion colour options with a 14-litre fuel tank and approximately 25 to 28 kmpl efficiency, the MT-03 is priced at approximately Rs 4.60 lakh to Rs 4.75 lakh ex-showroom competing with KTM Duke 390, BMW G310R and Kawasaki Z400. 
 - The MT-03's twin-cylinder smoothness, Yamaha MT brand heritage, accessible yet genuinely exciting power delivery and strong long-term reliability make it a compelling choice for riders transitioning from smaller displacement bikes into the middleweight naked segment.
competitor_vehicles: KTM Duke 390, Honda CB300R, Kawasaki Z400

feature_summary:
The Yamaha FZ25 is a quarter-litre naked street motorcycle powered by a 249cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke, 2-valve single-cylinder engine producing 20.8 PS at 8,000 rpm and 20.1 Nm at 6,000 rpm, paired with a 5-speed gearbox, delivering strong low and mid-range torque well suited for both city commuting and weekend highway touring. 
 - The motorcycle features a steel Deltabox frame with telescopic front forks, a mono-shock rear linkage suspension, a 282 mm front disc and 220 mm rear disc brakes with single-channel ABS (front only), 17-inch alloy wheels fitted with 100/80 front and 140/60 rear tubeless tyres ensuring stable and predictable handling on Indian road conditions. 
 - A fully digital LCD instrument cluster with gear position indicator, speed, RPM, fuel gauge, odometer, tripmeter and clock, along with full LED headlamp, LED tail lamp and LED indicators, make the FZ25 a well-equipped 250cc naked motorcycle with a modern technology presentation. 
 - The FZ25 is engineered for long-distance comfort with a 14-litre fuel tank, a claimed efficiency of approximately 40 kmpl, a wide and comfortable seat, an upright relaxed riding ergonomy and a wide handlebar grip making it practical for commuting and interstate touring alike. 
 - Available in Racing Blue, Dark Matte Blue and Metallic Black colour options, the FZ25 is priced at approximately Rs 1.35 lakh to Rs 1.40 lakh ex-showroom, competing with Hero Xtreme 250R and Suzuki Gixxer 250 in the 250cc naked segment. 
 - Compared to rivals, the FZ25 stands out for its combination of accessible Yamaha reliability, a strong mid-range torque character, the practical air-cooled format eliminating coolant maintenance complexity and competitive pricing that makes 250cc performance genuinely accessible for everyday Indian riders.
competitor_vehicles: Honda CB300F, KTM Duke 250, Bajaj Pulsar N250

major_changes: Semi-faired variant of FZ25 with sporty front cowl
feature_summary:
The Yamaha FZS 25 is the premium variant of the FZ25, sharing the same 249cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke single-cylinder engine producing 20.8 PS at 8,000 rpm and 20.1 Nm at 6,000 rpm with 5-speed gearbox, but adding dual-channel ABS, exclusive dual-tone paint schemes and sporty decals that differentiate it from the base FZ25. 
 - The cycle parts include the Deltabox steel frame, telescopic front forks, mono-shock rear, 282 mm front disc and 220 mm rear disc with dual-channel ABS as the key upgrade over the single-channel ABS of the base FZ25, 17-inch alloy wheels with 100/80 front and 140/60 rear tubeless tyres delivering improved braking confidence for mixed urban and highway use. 
 - The fully digital instrument cluster with gear position indicator, full LED lighting package, USB charging port, comfortable upright ergonomics and 14-litre fuel tank with approximately 40 kmpl efficiency are all retained from the FZ25, with the FZS 25 adding visual differentiation for riders who want a more premium appearance. 
 - The FZS 25 is positioned as the more complete and safety-focused choice within the FZ25 family, with dual-channel ABS providing superior rear brake modulation and improved stopping stability on varied road surfaces compared to the front-only ABS on the base FZ25. 
 - Available in exclusive dual-tone colour combinations not offered on the base FZ25, the FZS 25 is priced at approximately Rs 1.41 lakh to Rs 1.47 lakh ex-showroom — a modest premium that makes the dual-channel ABS upgrade an excellent value proposition for safety-conscious quarter-litre buyers. 
 - Compared with the Suzuki Gixxer 250, Hero Xtreme 250R and Honda CB200X (different segment), the FZS 25 delivers Yamaha's proven reliability, dual-channel ABS safety, 250cc performance and the practical air-cooled format, making it the preferred choice for budget-conscious buyers who don't want to compromise on braking technology.
competitor_vehicles: Honda CB300F, KTM Duke 250, Bajaj Pulsar RS200

remarks: Premium stylish scooter with retro-modern design
feature_summary:

remarks: Sporty street-style scooter targeting youth segment
feature_summary:
The Yamaha Ray ZR 125 Fi is a sporty, street-rally inspired 125cc scooter powered by a 125cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke Blue Core engine producing 8.2 PS at 6,500 rpm and 10.3 Nm at 5,000 rpm, with Yamaha's Smart Motor Generator (SMG) for silent starts and a claimed fuel efficiency of approximately 66 kmpl, targeting young urban buyers who want attitude and efficiency together.

vehicle_model_name: Ray ZR Street Rally 125 Fi Hybrid
vehicle_model_aliases: Ray ZR Hybrid, Ray ZR Street Rally
major_changes: Smart Motor Generator hybrid technology, improved mileage
remarks: India's first hybrid scooter with SMG technology
feature_summary:
The Yamaha Ray ZR Street Rally 125 Fi Hybrid is the most advanced variant in the Ray ZR family, powered by a 125cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke Blue Core engine integrated with a Smart Motor Generator (SMG) hybrid system producing 8.2 PS and 10.3 Nm, delivering a class-leading claimed efficiency of approximately 66 to 70 kmpl through energy recovery during braking and deceleration. 
 - The SMG hybrid system uses the generator unit to both assist engine acceleration using stored energy and recover kinetic energy during braking phases, reducing the combustion engine's load during acceleration and resulting in measurably better fuel economy and lower emissions compared to pure combustion-only scooters in this segment. 
 - It features Bluetooth Y-Connect app connectivity with real-time call and SMS alerts and trip data, a fully digital instrument console showing hybrid mode status, battery charge indicator, speed, fuel level and odometer, a USB type-A charging port and full LED lighting with an LED headlamp and LED tail lamp. 
 - The Street Rally styling with dual-tone aggressive graphics, sporty LED headlamp cluster with DRL, a sporty seat design and bold street rally badging make the Ray ZR Street Rally Hybrid the most visually striking variant in the 125cc scooter segment, appealing strongly to young eco-conscious urban riders. 
 - It rides on 12-inch alloy wheels with 90/90 front and 100/80 rear tubeless tyres, telescopic front suspension and unit swing rear suspension, with an optional 220 mm front disc brake and rear drum with combi-brake system, and a 5.2-litre fuel tank with a 99 kg kerb weight for agile city manoeuvrability. 
 - Priced at approximately Rs 86,000 to Rs 92,000 ex-showroom, the Ray ZR Street Rally 125 Fi Hybrid commands a slight premium over the non-hybrid variant and is unique in the 125cc segment for its genuine electro-mechanical hybrid technology, making it the strongest choice for eco-forward buyers who want the most advanced urban scooter in Yamaha's lineup.
competitor_vehicles: TVS NTorq 125, Honda Activa 125, Suzuki Avenis

major_changes: 155cc VVA maxi-scooter, traction control, dual-channel ABS
remarks: Premium maxi-scooter with sporty motorcycle-like performance
feature_summary:
The Yamaha Aerox 155 is a premium performance maxi-scooter powered by a 155cc liquid-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke, 4-valve DOHC single-cylinder engine with Variable Valve Actuation (VVA) technology producing 15 PS at 8,000 rpm and 13.9 Nm at 6,500 rpm, paired with a CVT automatic transmission — the same engine powering the MT-15 V2 — making it the fastest and most powerful scooter in the Indian 150cc-plus segment. 
 - The Aerox 155 uses a trellis-style frame as a first-in-class engineering choice for a scooter in India, with 13-inch front and 12-inch rear disc brakes with dual-channel ABS, telescopic front forks, a unit swing rear suspension and 110/70-13 front and 130/70-12 rear tubeless tyres for genuinely dynamic, scooter-defying handling. 
 - Bluetooth Y-Connect app connectivity with a full-colour TFT instrument display showing speed, tachometer, fuel gauge, riding mode, VVA indicator and Bluetooth call and navigation information makes the Aerox 155 the most connected and technology-rich scooter in Yamaha's India lineup. 
 - Styling derived from Yamaha's international XMAX maxi-scooter features twin LED projector headlamps, full LED lighting, a sleek aerodynamic front fairing, LED tail lamps, a keyless ignition with answer-back security and a 22.3-litre under-seat storage space accommodating a full-face helmet for practical premium usability. 
 - Available in Matte Red, Matte Blue, Matte Black and Metallic Black with a 5.5-litre fuel tank offering approximately 35 to 40 kmpl efficiency and an upright sporty riding position, the Aerox 155 is priced at approximately Rs 1.44 lakh to Rs 1.58 lakh ex-showroom. 
 - Compared to Aprilia SR 160 and TVS NTorq 125 Race Edition, the Aerox 155 outclasses all rivals in outright performance, premium features, XMAX-derived international styling and technology, making it the definitive performance scooter choice for buyers who want motorcycle-grade performance and features in an automatic scooter format.
competitor_vehicles: TVS NTorq 125, Honda Grazia 125, Aprilia SR 160

major_changes: Smart Motor Generator hybrid tech added to Fascino 125
remarks: Hybrid variant of the popular Fascino 125 with improved efficiency
feature_summary:
The Yamaha Fascino 125 Fi Hybrid is the eco-premium variant of the Fascino 125 lineup, powered by a 125cc air-cooled, fuel-injected Blue Core engine integrated with Yamaha's Smart Motor Generator (SMG) hybrid technology producing 8.2 PS and 10.3 Nm, delivering an exceptional claimed fuel efficiency of approximately 66 to 68 kmpl — among the best in any scooter sold in India today. 
 - The SMG hybrid system captures kinetic energy during braking and deceleration, storing it to assist the engine during acceleration, which reduces fuel consumption and enables whisper-quiet, vibration-free restarts without the conventional starter motor noise associated with traditional scooters in this class. 
 - Features include Bluetooth Y-Connect app connectivity with call and SMS alerts and ride data, a fully digital instrument cluster showing hybrid system status and battery charge indicator, a USB type-A charging port, full LED lighting with headlamp and DRL, LED tail lamp and LED indicators for a complete modern feature package.

 - Priced at approximately Rs 84,000 to Rs 92,000 ex-showroom and competing with Honda Activa 125 H-Smart and TVS Jupiter 125 SmartXonnect, the Fascino 125 Fi Hybrid's genuine SMG hybrid technology, superior fuel efficiency and Italian-inspired styling are its primary competitive differentiators in the premium 125cc scooter segment.
competitor_vehicles: Honda Activa 125, TVS Jupiter 125, Suzuki Access 125

remarks: Discontinued budget scooter replaced by newer models
feature_summary:
The Yamaha Alpha is an entry-level 113cc automatic scooter powered by a 113cc air-cooled, 4-stroke, 2-valve single-cylinder carburetted engine producing approximately 7.1 PS at 7,500 rpm and 8.1 Nm of torque, paired with a CVT automatic transmission, designed as an affordable and reliable urban scooter for budget-conscious buyers seeking Yamaha quality at the lowest accessible price. 
 - The Alpha features a conventional round headlamp, a practical underseat storage compartment, a flat floorboard for ease of boarding, telescopic front suspension and unit swing rear suspension, with a front disc or drum brake option and rear drum brake with combi-braking system for basic but safe everyday stopping performance. 
 - Yamaha's Blue Core engine efficiency delivers a claimed fuel economy of approximately 55 to 60 kmpl alongside a 5.2-litre fuel tank, making the Alpha's operational costs among the lowest of any Yamaha product and especially practical for buyers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets where fuel cost sensitivity is high. 
 - The instrument cluster is an analogue setup with speedometer, fuel gauge and warning lights reflecting the Alpha's positioning as a no-frills entry-level product, while 10-inch alloy wheels with tubeless tyres provide stable manoeuvrability in congested city traffic with minimal maintenance requirements. 
 - Available in standard colour options for the entry-level scooter segment, the Alpha is primarily sold in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities and rural markets where its affordability, Yamaha brand trust and low maintenance costs are the dominant purchase drivers. 
 - Priced at approximately Rs 60,000 to Rs 67,000 ex-showroom, the Alpha competes with Honda Activa i, TVS Scooty Zest and Hero Destini 110 at the entry-level scooter end of the market, where Yamaha's engine reliability, build quality and strong dealer network give it a meaningful quality advantage over less established brands.

major_changes: BS4 version, replaced by Fascino 125 FI under BS6
feature_summary:
The Yamaha Fascino (original 113cc variant) is an elegantly styled entry-level automatic scooter powered by a 113cc air-cooled, 4-stroke, 2-valve carburetted engine producing approximately 7.1 PS at 7,500 rpm and 8.1 Nm of torque, paired with a CVT transmission, aimed at the style and value-conscious segment of the Indian scooter market with an Italian-inspired aesthetic. 
 - The Fascino's design was transformative at its launch, featuring smooth curved Italian-inspired lines, chrome accents, a wide sculpted seat, a retro-modern headlamp and an elegant overall aesthetic that fundamentally differentiated it from functionally styled rivals and pioneered the concept of the scooter as a fashion accessory in India. 
 - The scooter rides on 10-inch alloy wheels with tubeless tyres, telescopic front forks and unit swing rear suspension, with a front disc brake option and rear drum with combi-brake system, while the 5.2-litre fuel tank and Blue Core-derived efficiency deliver approximately 55 kmpl claimed fuel economy.
