competitor_vehicles: Honda Activa 3G, TVS Jupiter, Suzuki Access 125

remarks: One of India's best-selling commuter motorcycles
feature_summary:
The Honda Shine 125 is one of India's best-selling commuter motorcycles powered by a 124.7cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke, 2-valve single-cylinder engine producing 10.7 PS at 7,500 rpm and 11 Nm at 6,000 rpm, paired with a 5-speed gearbox, offering a dependable and refined commuting experience backed by Honda's legendary reliability and the advanced PGM-FI fuel injection system. 
 - The Shine 125 features Honda's 4-step adjustable clutch lever for rider comfort in stop-and-go city traffic, a diamond type frame with telescopic front suspension and 5-step adjustable spring-loaded hydraulic rear suspension, a 240 mm front disc with CBS and rear drum with CBS delivering balanced and safe braking performance. 
 - Honda's ACG (Alternating Current Generator) starter system provides a silent, vibration-free engine start without starter motor clatter, while the fully digital instrument cluster shows speed, RPM, fuel level, odometer, two tripmeters, clock, service reminder and CBS indicator for comprehensive ride information. 
 - Full LED lighting including headlamp, tail lamp and position lamps, a long and comfortable split seat, upright riding ergonomics with a wide handlebar, and a 13-litre fuel tank with a claimed fuel efficiency of approximately 60 kmpl make the Shine 125 practical and economical for daily urban and semi-urban commuting. 
 - Available in Pearl Igneous Black, Matte Axis Grey Metallic, Radiant Red Metallic, Athletic Blue Metallic and Pearl Sporty Yellow colour options, the Shine 125 is priced at approximately Rs 82,000 to Rs 88,000 ex-showroom competing with TVS Raider 125, Bajaj Pulsar 125 and Hero Super Splendor. 
 - Honda's fuel injection quality, ACG silent start, strong resale value, unmatched Honda service network depth and long-term engine reliability make the Shine 125 one of the most trusted 125cc commuter motorcycles in India, appealing consistently to practical-minded daily commuter buyers across all market tiers.
competitor_vehicles: Bajaj Platina 110, TVS Raider 125, Hero Glamour

feature_summary:
The Honda SP125 is a premium commuter motorcycle powered by a 124cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke OHC single-cylinder engine with Honda's eSP (Enhanced Smart Power) technology producing 10.7 PS at 7,500 rpm and 11 Nm at 6,000 rpm, mated to a 5-speed gearbox, engineered specifically for maximum fuel efficiency, low vibration and refined everyday performance. 
 - The eSP technology suite includes an ACG silent starter for vibration-free ignition, PGM-FI fuel injection, an offset cylinder design to reduce piston friction, a roller rocker arm for reduced valve train friction and an overall low-friction engine design delivering a class-leading claimed fuel efficiency of approximately 60 kmpl. 
 - The SP125 uses a diamond type frame with telescopic front forks, a 5-step preload adjustable rear hydraulic shock absorber, a 240 mm front disc with single-channel CBS and rear drum with CBS, a fully digital instrument console with all-LED lighting and a USB charging port — making it one of the most feature-complete 125cc commuters available. 
 - The Idling Stop System (ISS) is a standout feature that automatically shuts the engine off at prolonged stops such as traffic signals and restarts it instantly when the throttle is opened, reducing fuel wastage and tailpipe emissions during urban stop-and-go commuting. 
 - Available in Pearl Igneous Black, Athletic Blue Metallic, Matte Axis Grey Metallic and Radiant Red Metallic in two variants, the SP125 is priced at approximately Rs 90,000 to Rs 96,000 ex-showroom competing with TVS Raider 125, Hero Super Splendor 125 i3S and Yamaha Saluto 125. 
 - The SP125's eSP technology package including ACG silent start, Idling Stop System, fuel injection precision, all-LED lighting and USB charging combine to deliver a genuinely premium commuter ownership experience that clearly justifies its price premium over basic 125cc rivals through real-world fuel savings and refined daily comfort.
competitor_vehicles: TVS Raider 125, Bajaj Pulsar 125, Hero Glamour

feature_summary:
The Honda Unicorn is a legendary commuter motorcycle powered in its current form by a 162.71cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke OHC single-cylinder engine producing 12.7 PS at 7,500 rpm and 14.4 Nm at 5,500 rpm, paired with a 5-speed gearbox, delivering Honda's trademark refinement and dependability for everyday commuting backed by a heritage dating back to the original Unicorn launched in 2004. 
 - The Unicorn features Honda's PGM-FI fuel injection for consistent throttle response and reliable cold-start performance, the ACG silent starter for smooth vibration-free ignition, a diamond type steel frame with telescopic front forks and twin rear hydraulic shock absorbers, 276 mm front disc with CBS and rear drum with CBS. 
 - A fully digital instrument cluster, full LED headlamp, LED tail lamp and LED indicators present a modern feature set, while 18-inch wheels with 80/100 front and 110/80 rear tubeless tyres, an upright and relaxed riding position with a comfortable seat and wide handlebar give the Unicorn its reputation as a relaxed, long-distance-friendly commuter. 
 - The 13-litre fuel tank delivers an excellent practical range with a claimed efficiency of approximately 50 to 55 kmpl, while the Unicorn's clean, understated design language with modern evolutionary styling appeals to mature, practical buyers who prioritise long-term reliability over flashy aesthetics. 
 - Available in Pearl Igneous Black, Matte Axis Grey Metallic, Radiant Red Metallic and Matte Marvel Blue Metallic, the Unicorn is priced at approximately Rs 1.08 lakh to Rs 1.12 lakh ex-showroom competing with Bajaj Pulsar 150, TVS Apache RTR 160 and Hero Xtreme 160R. 
 - Honda's legendary engine longevity, refined power delivery, PGM-FI reliability, strong dealer network penetration and consistently high resale value make the Honda Unicorn one of the most trusted long-term investments in the 150 to 165cc commuter motorcycle segment in India.
competitor_vehicles: Bajaj Pulsar 150, TVS Apache RTR 160, Yamaha FZ FI

major_changes: New generation with full-LED lighting, dual-channel ABS
feature_summary:
The Honda Hornet 2.0 is a feature-rich sport-commuter motorcycle powered by a 184.4cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke OHC single-cylinder engine producing 17.03 PS at 8,500 rpm and 16.1 Nm at 6,000 rpm, paired with a 5-speed gearbox, positioned as Honda's most performance-focused commuter motorcycle in the sub-200cc class with class-first dual-channel ABS. 
 - The Hornet 2.0 features a 276 mm front disc and 220 mm rear disc with dual-channel ABS as a class-first feature in the 180cc-plus commuter segment, telescopic front forks, a mono-shock rear linkage suspension, 17-inch alloy wheels with 110/70 front and 140/70 rear tubeless tyres for a wider, sportier stance and confident handling. 
 - A fully digital instrument cluster with tachometer, speed, fuel gauge, gear indicator, odometer, tripmeter and service reminder, alongside full LED lighting with a sleek LED headlamp, LED tail lamp and LED indicators, make the Hornet 2.0 one of the most well-equipped 180cc sport commuters from a mainstream manufacturer. 
 - The bold street fighter styling with a muscular fuel tank, minimalist tail section, aggressive headlamp, sporty shroud design and Honda's ACG silent starter give the Hornet 2.0 an intimidating presence, while a USB type-A charging port, 12-litre fuel tank and approximately 45 kmpl efficiency ensure practical daily usability. 
 - Available in Matte Marvel Blue Metallic, Pearl Sports Yellow, Radiant Red Metallic and Matte Axis Grey Metallic, the Hornet 2.0 is priced at approximately Rs 1.34 lakh to Rs 1.40 lakh ex-showroom competing with Yamaha FZ-S FI, TVS Apache RTR 160 4V and Bajaj Pulsar NS160. 
 - The Hornet 2.0's dual-channel ABS, Honda's engineering precision, sporty 184cc power output, street fighter styling and Honda's unmatched after-sales network make it the most safety-complete and brand-trustworthy performance commuter in the 160 to 185cc segment in India.
competitor_vehicles: Yamaha FZ FI, Bajaj Pulsar NS200, TVS Apache RTR 200 4V

remarks: Sporty 160cc street motorcycle with racing-inspired design
feature_summary:
The Honda X-Blade is a sporty 160cc street-fighter motorcycle powered by a 162.71cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke, 4-valve OHC single-cylinder engine producing 12.9 PS at 8,500 rpm and 14.6 Nm at 6,000 rpm, paired with a 5-speed gearbox, positioned with sharp, aggressive X-signature LED styling and a feature set specifically targeting young sporty buyers. 
 - The XBlade features a 276 mm front disc with CBS and rear drum with CBS, telescopic front forks and a mono-shock rear linkage suspension, 17-inch alloy wheels with 100/80 front and 130/70 rear tubeless tyres giving it a wide and aggressive stance, along with Honda's ACG silent starter for smooth vibration-free ignition. 
 - The full LED headlamp with sharp DRLs, LED tail lamp, LED indicators and a fully digital instrument console with speedometer, tachometer, fuel gauge, gear indicator and odometer make the XBlade's feature list comparable to more expensive naked motorcycles in adjacent displacement segments. 
 - Styling is the XBlade's strongest asset with its X-shaped LED headlamp signature, sharp tank extensions, edgy body panels, muscular fuel tank and X-shaped LED tail lamp creating a coherent and genuinely aggressive visual identity that successfully differentiates it from more conservatively styled commuter rivals. 
 - Available in Striking Blue, Matte Axis Grey Metallic, Pearl Igneous Black and Red with a 12-litre fuel tank and approximately 45 to 50 kmpl claimed efficiency, the XBlade is priced at approximately Rs 1.13 lakh to Rs 1.20 lakh ex-showroom competing with Yamaha FZ FI, Hero Xtreme 160R and Bajaj Pulsar 150 Neon. 
 - The XBlade's X-signature LED lighting design, Honda quality, sporty 160cc character and aggressive street fighter aesthetics give it a distinctive identity in the crowded 150 to 160cc sport commuter segment that strongly appeals to young buyers seeking premium styling at a practical commuter price.
competitor_vehicles: Yamaha FZ FI, TVS Apache RTR 160, Bajaj Pulsar NS160

feature_summary:
The Honda Livo is a refined entry-level 110cc commuter motorcycle powered by a 109.51cc air-cooled, 4-stroke, 2-valve OHC single-cylinder carburetted engine producing 8.23 PS at 7,500 rpm and 9.09 Nm at 5,500 rpm, mated to a 4-speed gearbox, engineered for practical, low-cost daily urban commuting with Honda's trademark reliability and the ACG silent starter as a premium feature. 
 - The Livo features Honda's ACG silent starter providing vibration-free and quiet engine ignition, a conventional diamond frame with leading link front suspension and twin rear shock absorbers for comfortable ride quality, and a front drum or disc brake with CBS and rear drum brake for safe and balanced stopping. 
 - Semi-analogue instrumentation with analogue speedometer and digital fuel gauge, 17-inch spoke or alloy wheels with 80/100 front and 80/100 rear tubeless tyres, chrome accents, a long comfortable seat and an upright riding position with wide handlebar give the Livo practical and accessible commuter ergonomics. 
 - A 10.5-litre fuel tank with a claimed fuel efficiency of approximately 65 kmpl delivers excellent operational economy, making the Livo one of the most cost-effective 110cc motorcycles from a running cost perspective for daily commuters in urban and rural markets. 
 - Available in Matte Axis Grey Metallic, Rebel Red Metallic, Pearl Igneous Black and Yellow, the Livo is priced at approximately Rs 75,000 to Rs 83,000 ex-showroom competing with Hero HF Deluxe, TVS Star City+ and Bajaj CT110. 
 - Honda's ACG silent start, brand trust, superior resale value and the wide Honda service network give the Livo a significant quality advantage over similarly priced rivals, making it the preferred choice for conservative buyers in Tier 2 and rural markets who prioritise long-term reliability and low total cost of ownership.
competitor_vehicles: Hero Splendor Plus, Bajaj Platina 110, TVS Star City+

feature_summary:
The Honda CD 110 Dream is Honda's most accessible commuter motorcycle in India, powered by a 109.51cc air-cooled, 4-stroke, 2-valve OHC single-cylinder carburetted engine producing 8.23 PS at 7,500 rpm and 9.09 Nm at 5,500 rpm, paired with a 4-speed gearbox, built to offer maximum fuel economy and the lowest total cost of ownership for the rural and semi-urban Indian buyer. 
 - The CD 110 Dream uses a conventional diamond frame with leading link front fork suspension and twin rear shock absorbers — a proven, simple setup that minimises maintenance requirements and maximises long-term durability even under heavy load and rough rural road conditions across India. 
 - Honda's ACG silent starter system is standard even on this budget model providing smooth, quiet engine starts — a comfort feature usually reserved for premium motorcycles but offered here as Honda's commitment to quality standards across all price points in its lineup. 
 - A front drum brake and rear drum brake with CBS on the DX variant, 17-inch steel spoke wheels with tube-type tyres chosen for low replacement cost, an analogue speedometer, wide comfortable seat, upright riding position and a practical rear carrier for load carrying make the CD 110 Dream the ideal working-class commuter for rural India. 
 - A 10.5-litre fuel tank with a claimed efficiency of approximately 65 to 70 kmpl delivers an exceptional practical range, making the CD 110 Dream one of the most economical motorcycles on Indian roads from both purchase and operational cost perspectives, with the two-variant lineup of D and DX offering different feature tiers. 
 - Available in Pearl Igneous Black, Matte Axis Grey Metallic, Rebel Red Metallic and Sports Yellow, priced at approximately Rs 68,000 to Rs 76,000 ex-showroom, competing with Hero HF Deluxe and Bajaj CT110 where Honda's ACG silent start, fuel efficiency, brand trust and superior service network depth are the defining advantages.
competitor_vehicles: Hero HF Dawn, Bajaj CT110, TVS Sport

remarks: Adventure-crossover positioned between commuter and middleweight
feature_summary:
The Honda CB200X is a crossover adventure-commuter motorcycle powered by a 184.4cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke OHC single-cylinder engine producing 17.03 PS at 8,500 rpm and 16.1 Nm at 6,000 rpm, paired with a 5-speed gearbox, designed to bridge urban commuting and lightweight adventure touring with raised suspension, crossover styling and genuine rough-road capability. 
 - The CB200X uses a steel diamond frame with 41 mm conventional telescopic front forks offering 145 mm travel and a preload adjustable mono-shock rear with 130 mm travel — both tuned specifically for comfortable performance over rough roads, village lanes and mild trail surfaces typical of crossover Indian riding conditions. 
 - Dual-channel ABS with a 276 mm front disc and 220 mm rear disc, 17-inch front and rear alloy wheels with wire-spoke styling and semi-knobby pattern tubeless tyres, an 810 mm seat height, a compact windscreen deflector, a round LED headlamp with DRL guards and aluminium-finish engine guard contribute to the CB200X's genuine adventure crossover character. 
 - The fully digital instrument console, full LED lighting, USB charging port, wide handlebar for easy off-road-inspired control and a comfortable upright riding position with a single-piece well-cushioned seat make the CB200X as practical as it is adventure-styled for everyday riding. 
 - A 12-litre fuel tank with approximately 45 kmpl efficiency gives the CB200X a practical touring range for inter-city journeys, with the shared Hornet 2.0 engine providing a proven and well-supported powertrain backed by Honda's extensive service infrastructure. 
 - Priced at approximately Rs 1.46 lakh to Rs 1.52 lakh ex-showroom, the CB200X competes with Yamaha FZ-X, Hero Xpulse 200 4V and Royal Enfield Meteor where Honda's dual-channel ABS, 184cc proven engine performance, crossover capability and build quality make it one of the most complete adventure crossover motorcycles under Rs 1.5 lakh.
competitor_vehicles: Yamaha FZ-X, Hero XPulse 200, Royal Enfield Hunter 350

feature_summary:
The Honda CB300F is a premium naked street motorcycle powered by a 293cc liquid-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke DOHC 4-valve single-cylinder engine producing 26.0 PS at 8,500 rpm and 25.9 Nm at 6,000 rpm, mated to a 6-speed gearbox with assist and slipper clutch, positioned as Honda's most accessible premium naked motorcycle in the sub-300cc segment with full-blown sports-naked character. 
 - The cycle parts include a steel trellis diamond frame with 37 mm conventional telescopic front forks, a preload adjustable mono-shock rear, a 296 mm front disc and 220 mm rear disc with dual-channel ABS, 17-inch alloy wheels with 110/70 front and 150/60 rear tubeless radial tyres for sharp and confident handling dynamics. 
 - A 5-inch colour TFT instrument display, Honda Riding Modes (Standard and Sport), Honda Selectable Torque Control (HSTC), full LED lighting with a Y-shaped DRL headlamp signature, a USB charging port and the assist and slipper clutch make the CB300F one of the most technology-loaded 300cc naked motorcycles from a mainstream manufacturer. 
 - The sportily upright ergonomics with a medium-width handlebar, rearward footpeg placement and an 820 mm seat height create a sporty but accessible riding position that appeals to riders upgrading from smaller motorcycles while remaining genuinely engaging for experienced sport riders. 
 - Available in Radiant Red Metallic, Pearl Igneous Black and Mat Axis Gray Metallic with a 12-litre fuel tank and approximately 30 to 35 kmpl efficiency, the CB300F is priced at approximately Rs 2.78 lakh to Rs 2.90 lakh ex-showroom competing with KTM Duke 250, Bajaj Dominar 250 and TVS Apache RR 310. 
 - The CB300F's TFT display, riding modes, traction control, liquid-cooled DOHC engine, assist and slipper clutch and Honda's premium brand experience combine to deliver a genuinely complete sub-300cc naked package that outclasses air-cooled rivals in technology sophistication and riding dynamics.
competitor_vehicles: Yamaha FZ25, KTM Duke 250, Bajaj Pulsar N250

feature_summary:
The Honda CB300R is a neo-retro styled premium naked motorcycle powered by a 286cc liquid-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke DOHC 4-valve single-cylinder engine producing approximately 31 PS at 9,000 rpm and 27.5 Nm at 7,500 rpm, paired with a 6-speed gearbox with assist and slipper clutch, combining Honda's CB café-racer heritage with thoroughly modern engineering and technology. 
 - The CB300R uses a steel trellis frame with 41 mm USD front forks for sharper steering response, a preload adjustable mono-shock rear, a 296 mm front disc and 240 mm rear disc with dual-channel ABS and Honda Selectable Torque Control (HSTC), 17-inch diamond-cut alloy wheels with 110/70 front and 150/60 rear radial tubeless tyres for premium handling capability. 
 - Honda Selectable Torque Control (HSTC) traction control, two riding modes, a round full-colour TFT instrument display with Bluetooth smartphone connectivity, a USB charging port and the assist and slipper clutch make the CB300R's feature set genuinely premium despite its accessible near-300cc displacement. 
 - The neo-retro design is the CB300R's defining identity — a circular LED headlamp with round DRL, an exposed trellis frame, minimalist bodywork, a short tail section, sculpted fuel tank and elegant proportions that reference Honda's classic CB café heritage while maintaining a thoroughly modern fit and finish quality. 
 - Available in Pearl Glare White, Mat Axis Gray Metallic and Matte Gunpowder Black Metallic with a 10-litre fuel tank and approximately 30 to 35 kmpl efficiency, the CB300R is priced at approximately Rs 2.93 lakh to Rs 3.05 lakh ex-showroom competing with KTM Duke 390, Husqvarna Vitpilen 401 and BMW G310R. 
 - The CB300R's neo-retro café-racer styling, USD forks, traction control, TFT Bluetooth display and Honda's premium brand experience at a near-300cc price point make it a uniquely compelling choice for style-conscious performance buyers who want genuine retro aesthetics without compromising on modern technology.
competitor_vehicles: KTM Duke 390, Yamaha MT-03, Kawasaki Z300

major_changes: Modern retro 350cc, Bluetooth connectivity, dual-channel ABS
remarks: Premium modern-retro 350cc competing with Royal Enfield
feature_summary:
The Honda H'ness CB350 is a premium modern-classic 350cc motorcycle powered by a 348.36cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke, 2-valve OHC single-cylinder engine producing 21.07 PS at 5,500 rpm and 30 Nm at 3,000 rpm, paired with a 5-speed gearbox, engineered to rival the Royal Enfield Meteor 350 with Honda's Japanese engineering precision, build quality and connected technology. 
 - The H'ness CB350 features dual-channel ABS, a 310 mm front disc and 240 mm rear disc, 41 mm conventional telescopic front forks and twin rear shock absorbers well-tuned for comfortable long-distance cruising, with a 800 mm seat height, wide handlebar, forward footpegs and a well-padded seat creating a relaxed and comfortable cruiser riding position. 
 - Honda Bluetooth Roadsynct connectivity is the standout modern feature, pairing the motorcycle with a smartphone app to display call and SMS notifications, music controls, turn-by-turn navigation prompts and trip data on the premium round analogue-digital instrument console — delivered to market before Royal Enfield added similar connectivity to the Meteor. 
 - The instrument console combines an analogue speedometer and tachometer with a central TFT display showing Bluetooth information, while the retro-round LED headlamp with DRL, LED tail lamp, LED indicators and chrome accents give the H'ness CB350 an unmistakably classic Honda CB aesthetic perfectly suited for the modern-classic buyer. 
 - Available in Pearl Igneous Black, Pearl Horizon White and Matte Axis Grey Metallic in two variants — DLX and DLX Pro — the H'ness CB350 is priced at approximately Rs 2.02 lakh to Rs 2.15 lakh ex-showroom competing with Royal Enfield Meteor 350 and Jawa Forty-Two. 
 - Honda's superior engine refinement, Roadsynct Bluetooth connectivity, dual-channel ABS, premium build quality and the Honda after-sales network depth are the H'ness CB350's primary competitive advantages over Royal Enfield's Meteor, making it the preferred choice for quality-conscious modern-classic buyers who value precision engineering alongside heritage styling.
competitor_vehicles: Royal Enfield Classic 350, Royal Enfield Meteor 350, Jawa 42

feature_summary:
The Honda CB350RS is the sporty café-racer inspired derivative of the H'ness CB350 platform, sharing the same 348.36cc air-cooled, fuel-injected OHC single-cylinder engine producing 21.07 PS and 30 Nm with a 5-speed gearbox, but distinguished by a darker, more aggressive styling with blacked-out components, golden fork stanchions, golden alloy wheels and a bolder visual identity. 
 - The CB350RS retains the H'ness CB350's complete mechanical specification including dual-channel ABS, 310 mm front disc, 240 mm rear disc, 41 mm telescopic front forks and twin rear shock absorbers, while differentiating through blacked-out engine casings, rounded exhaust muffler, sporty flyscreen and darker graphics for a more purposeful café-racer character. 
 - Honda Bluetooth Roadsynct is standard on the CB350RS, enabling smartphone connectivity for call and SMS alerts, turn-by-turn navigation on the TFT section of the analogue-TFT instrument console, music controls and ride data tracking, providing the same connected experience as the H'ness CB350 but with a sportier visual execution. 
 - The minimalist tail section, solo seat pad for a racing look, blacked-out tank with unique RS graphics and overall darker aesthetic compared to the classically elegant H'ness CB350 appeal strongly to the 25 to 35 age group who want café-racer attitude with Honda's engineering pedigree and reliability. 
 - Available in Pearl Igneous Black, Mat Axis Gray Metallic and Matte Steel Black Metallic exclusive to the RS, the CB350RS is priced at approximately Rs 2.03 lakh to Rs 2.17 lakh ex-showroom competing with Royal Enfield Meteor 350, Yezdi Roadster and Jawa Perak. 
 - The CB350RS uniquely combines Honda's engine refinement and Roadsynct Bluetooth connectivity with a genuinely distinct café-racer aesthetic, making it the strongest option in the modern-retro 350cc segment for buyers who want the H'ness CB350 platform's proven quality expressed through a bolder and more spirited visual character.
competitor_vehicles: Royal Enfield Meteor 350, Jawa Perak, Honda H'ness CB350

major_changes: Updated CB350 with new design language and features
remarks: Latest generation of the CB350 family
feature_summary:
The Honda CB350 new generation refers to the updated and refined versions of the CB350 platform, continuing to use the proven 348.36cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke OHC single-cylinder engine producing 21.07 PS at 5,500 rpm and 30 Nm at 3,000 rpm, paired with a 5-speed gearbox, with Honda incorporating riding dynamic refinements, updated technology and new colour and graphics options based on customer feedback from the earlier H'ness and RS variants. 
 - The new generation CB350 retains dual-channel ABS, a 310 mm front disc, 240 mm rear disc, 41 mm telescopic front forks and twin rear shock absorbers, while benefiting from updated fuel injection calibration for improved throttle response, refined suspension tuning for better composure on Indian roads and updated software for the Bluetooth Roadsynct connectivity system. 
 - Honda Bluetooth Roadsynct connectivity with call and SMS notifications, turn-by-turn navigation, music controls and trip data remains standard, while the analogue-TFT hybrid instrument cluster continues to deliver a premium blend of retro character and modern digital functionality valued by modern-classic buyers. 
 - New generation updates bring improved riding mode options, potential Honda Selectable Torque Control on select variants, updated colour and graphics reflecting current market trends and refined ergonomic details that keep the CB350 platform competitive against Royal Enfield's continuously evolving Hunter 350 and Classic 350 lineup. 
 - The 15-litre fuel tank, approximately 45 to 50 kmpl efficiency, comfortable 800 mm seat height and relaxed cruiser ergonomics ensure the new generation CB350 continues to excel as both a premium daily motorcycle and a weekend touring modern-classic machine. 
 - Priced at approximately Rs 2.10 lakh to Rs 2.25 lakh ex-showroom for updated variants competing with Royal Enfield Meteor 350, Hunter 350 and Classic 350, the new generation CB350's combination of Honda engineering precision, connectivity and genuine premium build quality makes it the most refined choice in the fast-growing 350cc modern-classic motorcycle segment.
competitor_vehicles: Royal Enfield Classic 350, Jawa 42, Honda H'ness CB350

major_changes: Successor to CB500X with updated styling
feature_summary:
The Honda NX500 is a mid-size adventure touring motorcycle powered by a 471cc liquid-cooled, parallel twin, 4-stroke DOHC fuel-injected engine producing 46.9 PS at 8,500 rpm and 43.4 Nm at 6,250 rpm, paired with a 6-speed gearbox with assist and slipper clutch, designed to conquer urban roads and adventurous weekend touring routes with genuine twin-cylinder refinement and ADV capability. 
 - The NX500 uses a steel twin-spar frame with 41 mm USD front forks offering 150 mm travel, a preload adjustable link mono-shock rear with 145 mm travel, a 310 mm front disc and 240 mm rear disc with dual-channel ABS, 19-inch front and 17-inch rear wire-spoke wheels with adventure-suitable dual-purpose tyres for genuine light off-road readiness. 
 - Honda Smartphone Voice Control System (HSVCS), a 5-inch TFT colour instrument panel with Bluetooth and smartphone integration, Honda Selectable Torque Control (HSTC) traction control, Urban and Tour riding modes, a DC power supply and a 12V power socket make the NX500 a well-connected and technology-complete adventure tourer. 
 - The adventure styling includes a robust beak front fender, a large height-adjustable windscreen, wide handlebars with hand guards, wire-spoke wheels, knuckle guards, an engine protection bar, aluminium footpegs and an 820 mm seat height — all contributing to a genuine adventure tourer identity suited for mixed on and off-road use. 
 - A 17.7-litre fuel tank provides a touring range of approximately 300 to 350 km per fill, with Honda's parallel twin delivering a broad, flexible power band equally suited for city traffic and sustained highway cruising, available in Matt Gunpowder Black Metallic and Pearl Glare White. 
 - Priced at approximately Rs 5.26 lakh to Rs 5.50 lakh ex-showroom in India, the NX500 competes with Royal Enfield Himalayan 450, KTM Adventure 390 and Suzuki V-Strom SX, where Honda's twin-cylinder refinement, TFT Bluetooth connectivity, traction control and genuine adventure touring capability justify its premium positioning in the accessible mid-size ADV segment.
competitor_vehicles: Kawasaki Versys 650, Suzuki V-Strom 650, BMW F 750 GS

remarks: Mid-weight adventure tourer, now succeeded by NX500
feature_summary:
The Honda CB500X is a versatile adventure touring motorcycle powered by a 471cc liquid-cooled, parallel twin, 4-stroke DOHC fuel-injected engine producing 46.5 PS at 8,500 rpm and 43.2 Nm at 6,500 rpm, paired with a 6-speed gearbox with assist and slipper clutch, designed as an accessible, broadly capable adventure touring motorcycle suited to both novice and experienced riders. 
 - The CB500X uses a steel twin-spar frame with 41 mm USD front forks offering 150 mm travel, a link-type mono-shock rear, 320 mm front disc and 240 mm rear disc with dual-channel ABS, 19-inch front and 17-inch rear spoke wheels with dual-purpose tyres for genuine light off-road capability on gravel and unpaved trails. 
 - Honda Selectable Torque Control (HSTC), multiple riding modes, a 5-inch TFT colour display with Bluetooth smartphone connectivity, Honda's Smartphone Voice Control System and a USB charging port provide a comprehensive and connected technology suite that makes the CB500X feel genuinely premium in its class. 
 - Adventure ergonomics include an 830 mm seat height, wide handlebars for easy control on rough terrain, hand guards, a large adjustable windscreen with strong wind protection, an upright relaxed touring position and an engine protection guard making it ready for trail use directly from the factory. 
 - A 17.7-litre fuel tank with approximately 25 to 30 kmpl efficiency delivers over 400 km touring range, with the smooth and torquey parallel twin renowned for linear, predictable power delivery that makes it exceptionally approachable for less experienced riders while remaining engaging for touring enthusiasts. 
 - Available in Matt Gunpowder Black Metallic, Pearl Glare White and Mat Axis Gray Metallic and priced at approximately Rs 8.50 lakh to Rs 9.50 lakh ex-showroom in India as a CBU import, the CB500X competes with Kawasaki Versys 650 and Suzuki V-Strom 650 where Honda's A2-licence-friendly pedigree, twin-cylinder refinement and TFT connectivity are its strongest draws.
competitor_vehicles: Kawasaki Versys 650, Suzuki V-Strom 650, Honda NX500

major_changes: New winglets, sharpened bodywork, revised ergonomics
remarks: Inline-4 sports tourer with everyday usability
feature_summary:
The Honda CBR650R is a premium fully-faired middleweight sports motorcycle powered by a 649cc inline four-cylinder, liquid-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke DOHC engine producing 95 PS at 12,000 rpm and 64 Nm at 8,500 rpm, mated to a 6-speed gearbox with assist and slipper clutch, delivering a genuine inline-four sports motorcycle experience with accessible everyday usability. 
 - The CBR650R uses a steel diamond frame with 41 mm Showa SFF-CA USD front forks, a preload adjustable Showa mono-shock rear, 310 mm dual front discs with radial-mount Nissin 4-piston calipers and a 240 mm rear disc with dual-channel ABS plus Honda Selectable Torque Control (HSTC), 17-inch forged alloy wheels with 120/70 front and 180/55 rear radial tyres. 
 - Sport, Standard and Rain riding modes via Honda Riding Mode Select, HSTC traction control, a full-colour 5-inch TFT instrument display with Bluetooth connectivity, LED twin headlamps with Fireblade-inspired dual fairing ducts and full LED lighting make the CBR650R a genuinely premium and well-equipped mid-class sports motorcycle. 
 - The inline-four engine character with its rev-hungry high-rpm power delivery and a distinctive four-cylinder crescendo up to 12,000 rpm provides the addictive inline-four sports experience that is Honda's hallmark from the CB750 to the RC213V-S, making the CBR650R special among mid-sized sports motorcycles. 
 - Available in Grand Prix Red and Matt Gunpowder Black Metallic with a 15.4-litre fuel tank and approximately 20 to 25 kmpl efficiency under mixed conditions, the CBR650R is priced at approximately Rs 9.50 lakh to Rs 10.20 lakh ex-showroom in India competing with Kawasaki Z650 and Yamaha MT-07. 
 - The CBR650R is the definitive choice for riders seeking the unique thrill of an inline-four sports motorcycle with accessible power, daily usability, Fireblade-inspired styling, riding modes, traction control and Honda's world-class four-cylinder engineering pedigree in one compelling and complete package.
competitor_vehicles: Kawasaki Ninja 650, Yamaha R6, Suzuki GSX-S750

facelift_description: New Neo Sports Café styling update
remarks: Neo Sports Café naked derived from CBR650R
feature_summary:
The Honda CB650R is the naked street fighter variant of the CBR650R, sharing the same 649cc inline four-cylinder, liquid-cooled, fuel-injected DOHC engine producing 95 PS at 12,000 rpm and 64 Nm at 8,500 rpm with 6-speed gearbox and assist and slipper clutch, but clothed in minimalist Neo-Sports Café styling that blends neo-retro aesthetics with Honda's modern engineering precision. 
 - The CB650R shares the CBR650R's premium cycle parts including the steel diamond frame, 41 mm Showa SFF-CA USD front forks, preload adjustable Showa mono-shock rear, 310 mm dual front discs with Nissin 4-piston radial calipers, 240 mm rear disc with dual-channel ABS and HSTC, and the naked format uses the exposed engine and frame as design elements. 
 - Sport, Standard and Rain riding modes, HSTC traction control, a full-colour 5-inch TFT instrument display with Bluetooth smartphone connectivity and full LED lighting are all standard, matching the CBR650R in technology while delivering a completely different Neo-Sports Café aesthetic character. 
 - The CB650R's Neo-Sports Café design features a round LED headlamp with circular DRL ring, an exposed engine area, minimalist tail unit, sculpted fuel tank, premium alloy wheels and elegant proportions that reference Honda's classic CB café heritage while maintaining thoroughly modern material quality and precision. 
 - Available in Candy Chromosphere Red and Matt Gunpowder Black Metallic with a 15.4-litre fuel tank and approximately 20 to 25 kmpl efficiency, the CB650R is priced at approximately Rs 9.40 lakh to Rs 10.00 lakh ex-showroom competing with Kawasaki Z650, Triumph Street Triple and Yamaha MT-07. 
 - The CB650R's combination of inline-four excitement and refinement, Neo-Sports Café retro styling, USD forks, traction control, TFT Bluetooth display and Honda's premium brand experience make it one of the most desirable naked motorcycles in its class for riders who want inline-four thrills in a beautiful, technology-forward package.
competitor_vehicles: Kawasaki Z650, Yamaha MT-07, Suzuki GSX-S750

facelift_description: Complete redesign in 2018, DCT gearbox option
major_changes: Flat-6 engine, DCT automatic option, Apple CarPlay, airbag
feature_summary:
The Honda Gold Wing is Honda's legendary flagship grand touring motorcycle, powered in its current Tour DCT form by a 1,833cc horizontally-opposed flat-six liquid-cooled, fuel-injected SOHC engine producing 125.7 PS at 5,500 rpm and 170 Nm at 4,500 rpm, mated to a 7-speed Dual Clutch Transmission (DCT), representing five decades of Honda touring excellence and the pinnacle of long-distance motorcycling comfort and technology. 
 - The Gold Wing's engineering is without precedent in production motorcycles — the horizontally mounted flat-six engine acts as a stressed chassis member, double-wishbone front suspension unique among motorcycles, electric power steering, an electronically adjustable semi-active suspension and an Airbag system on the Tour Airbag variant demonstrate Honda's absolute commitment to innovation over production cost. 
 - Apple CarPlay integration on a 7-inch Android-based touchscreen, Bluetooth audio with a premium 6-speaker sound system, heated seats, heated grips, a reverse gear function, electric power steering, cruise control, Tour and Sport and Econ riding modes and a fully integrated navigation system make the Gold Wing effectively a luxury touring vehicle on two wheels. 
 - The DCT Dual Clutch Transmission offers fully automatic shifting with manual paddle overrides, a Walking Mode for ultra-slow garage manoeuvrability and a dedicated Tour mode for long-distance fuel efficiency optimisation — technology derived directly from Honda's car engineering division and refined specifically for the Gold Wing's unique character. 
 - The Gold Wing Tour variant adds an integrated top case and saddlebags with 110 litres of total storage, an electrically adjustable touring screen and additional comfort features, while the total wet weight of approximately 365 kg is managed through the advanced chassis engineering, DCT and electric power steering making it more accessible than its size suggests. 
 - Available in Candy Ardent Red, Pearl Glare White and Mat Gunpowder Black Metallic with a 21-litre fuel tank and approximately 350 to 400 km touring range, the Gold Wing is priced at approximately Rs 38 to 39 lakh ex-showroom in India as a CBU, competing with BMW K1600 and Harley-Davidson touring models as the world's most comprehensively engineered luxury touring motorcycle.
competitor_vehicles: BMW K 1600 GTL, Harley-Davidson Electra Glide, Indian Roadmaster

facelift_description: 6th generation – new LED headlamp, updated body, BS6 engine
major_changes: BS6 OBD2 engine, new silent start ACG, mobile charging socket, updated instrument cluster
remarks: India's best-selling scooter for two decades; cornerstone of Honda's two-wheeler lineup
feature_summary:
The Honda Activa 6G is India's best-selling two-wheeler, powered by a 109.51cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke, 2-valve OHC single-cylinder engine producing 7.68 PS at 8,000 rpm and 8.79 Nm at 5,000 rpm, with Honda's ACG silent starter technology, BS6 Phase 2 compliance and OBD2 on-board diagnostics representing the latest evolution of an iconic product that has led the Indian scooter market for over two decades. 
 - The Activa 6G features an upgraded telescopic front suspension as a premium change from the earlier trailing link setup of previous generations, a 7-step adjustable spring-loaded rear shock absorber, a 130 mm front drum brake or optional disc with CBS and a 130 mm rear drum with CBS, and 10-inch tubeless alloy wheels for stable low-speed urban manoeuvrability. 
 - Honda's PGM-FI fuel injection with OBD2 diagnostics ensures consistent performance, emission compliance and easier service diagnostics, while the ACG starter provides vibration-free and whisper-quiet engine ignition and the semi-digital instrument console with analogue speedometer and digital fuel gauge presents essential riding information. 
 - Under-seat storage of 21 litres accommodates a half-face helmet, the 5.3-litre fuel tank with Honda's fuel injection delivers approximately 60 kmpl claimed efficiency, LED position lamp, halogen or LED headlamp options depending on variant, LED tail lamp and a split-type handle-lock improve the Activa 6G's everyday usability. 
 - Available in Pearl Precious White, Matte Axis Grey Metallic, Pearl Igneous Black, Pep Yellow, Rebel Red Metallic and Sports Red with a wide range of variant options, the Activa 6G is priced at approximately Rs 76,000 to Rs 82,000 ex-showroom competing with TVS Jupiter, Hero Destini 125 and Suzuki Access 125. 
 - The Activa 6G's Honda brand trust, unmatched resale value, cultural significance as India's most trusted two-wheeler, excellent dealer network depth, telescopic front suspension upgrade, OBD2 diagnostics and ACG silent start collectively make it the benchmark urban scooter that all other 110cc scooters are measured against in India.
competitor_vehicles: TVS Jupiter, Hero Destini 125, Suzuki Access 125

facelift_description: H-Smart key, OBD2 update, new colours
major_changes: BS6 OBD2 compliance, H-Smart keyless ignition, tyre pressure monitor on top variant
remarks: Premium 125cc scooter with advanced features over standard Activa
feature_summary:
The Honda Activa 125 is the premium flagship of the Activa family, powered by a 124cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke OHC single-cylinder engine with Honda's eSP+ (Enhanced Smart Power Plus) technology producing 8.2 PS at 6,500 rpm and 10.4 Nm at 5,000 rpm, offering a significantly more powerful, refined and feature-rich riding experience compared to the standard Activa 6G. 
 - The eSP+ technology includes an ACG silent starter, an Idling Stop System (ISS) that shuts the engine off at prolonged stops and restarts instantly when the throttle is opened, PGM-FI fuel injection and low-friction engine components, delivering a class-leading claimed fuel efficiency of approximately 60 to 63 kmpl while reducing urban tailpipe emissions. 
 - The Activa 125 features an optional front disc brake with Honda CBS, telescopic front suspension, a 7-step adjustable rear spring-loaded hydraulic suspension, 12-inch alloy wheels with tubeless tyres and a fully digital instrument console — clear upgrades over the base Activa 6G that justify the segment step-up. 
 - Bluetooth Smart H-Smart connectivity on the top variant enables call and SMS notifications, trip data and ride reminders through the connected instrument console, full LED lighting including headlamp, tail lamp and turn indicators, a USB type-A charging port and 21 litres of under-seat storage complete the Activa 125's premium feature package. 
 - Available in Pearl Igneous Black, Pearl Sparkling White, Mat Axis Grey Metallic, Rebel Red Metallic and Matte Steel Black Metallic in three variants — Std, Deluxe and H-Smart — the Activa 125 is priced at approximately Rs 84,000 to Rs 93,000 ex-showroom. 
 - Competing with TVS Jupiter 125 and Yamaha Fascino 125 Fi, the Honda Activa 125 stands out with its eSP+ technology including Idling Stop System, Bluetooth connectivity on H-Smart, Honda's superior after-sales network and the trust of the Activa brand name, making it the preferred premium 125cc scooter choice for Honda loyalists across India.
competitor_vehicles: TVS Jupiter 125, Suzuki Access 125, Yamaha Fascino 125

facelift_description: 2024 refresh – new colour options, updated graphics
major_changes: Upgraded to 125cc engine from legacy 110cc, BS6 OBD2, sporty redesign
remarks: Youth-focused sporty scooter; moved from 110cc to 125cc platform
feature_summary:
The Honda Dio 125 is a sporty, design-forward 125cc automatic scooter powered by a 123.94cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke OHC single-cylinder engine with Honda's eSP technology producing 8.18 PS at 6,500 rpm and 10.5 Nm at 5,000 rpm, featuring ACG silent start and PGM-FI fuel injection, targeting young urban buyers who equally prioritise cutting-edge styling and modern technology. 
 - Key features include a fully digital instrument console with digital speedometer, tachometer bar graph, fuel gauge, odometer and tripmeter, full LED lighting comprising headlamp, tail lamp and indicators, a USB type-A charging port and Honda's ACG silent starter — creating a premium technology experience at a competitive 125cc scooter price. 
 - The Dio 125 uses 12-inch alloy wheels with tubeless tyres, telescopic front suspension and a spring-loaded hydraulic rear shock absorber, with an optional front disc brake with CBS and rear drum with CBS, while the flat floorboard, 18-litre under-seat storage and an accessible 788 mm seat height make it practical for urban daily use. 
 - Design is the Dio 125's strongest differentiator — the distinctive sporty character features a sharp LED headlamp, edgy body panels, an X-shaped LED tail lamp element, sporty side cowl design and strong visual differentiation from the mainstream Activa family, clearly communicating its appeal to a younger, more fashion-conscious demographic. 
 - A 5.3-litre fuel tank delivering approximately 55 to 60 kmpl claimed efficiency, the ACG silent start and a sporty yet practical overall package make the Dio 125 a complete urban scooter for college-going youth and young professionals who want Honda reliability with genuinely distinctive sporty aesthetics. 
 - Available in Pearl Igneous Black, Matte Steel Black Metallic, Matte Sangria Red Metallic and Rebel Red Metallic, the Dio 125 is priced at approximately Rs 80,000 to Rs 87,000 ex-showroom competing with Yamaha Ray ZR 125 Fi, TVS NTorq 125 and Suzuki Avenis 125 where Honda's build quality and X-signature design language give it a loyal and growing following.
competitor_vehicles: TVS NTorq 125, Yamaha Ray ZR 125, Suzuki Avenis

facelift_description: Updated LED lighting, new colour options, BS6 OBD2
major_changes: BS6 OBD2 update, revised styling, new console
remarks: Premium urban scooter with under-seat storage and sleek styling
feature_summary:
The Honda Grazia 125 is a premium, feature-rich 125cc automatic scooter powered by a 124.9cc air-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke OHC single-cylinder engine with Honda's eSP technology producing approximately 8.5 PS at 6,500 rpm and 10.54 Nm at 5,000 rpm, positioned as a stylistically premium and technology-forward alternative to the Activa 125 targeting style-conscious urban buyers. 
 - The Grazia 125 was notable at launch for featuring a full LED headlamp as a class-first standard specification, an external fuel filler cap avoiding the need to open the seat for refuelling, a high-resolution fully digital instrument console with speed, tachometer bar graph, odometer, tripmeter, clock and fuel level display and Honda's ACG silent starter with PGM-FI injection. 
 - The scooter rides on 12-inch alloy wheels with tubeless tyres, telescopic front forks and a spring-loaded rear hydraulic shock absorber, with a front disc brake and CBS or front drum and CBS depending on variant, providing safe and predictable stopping performance for a lightweight premium 125cc scooter. 
 - A premium car-inspired dashboard design, sculpted sporty body panels with chrome accents, a distinctive tail section with LED tail lamps, a USB charging port and the external fuel filler lid give the Grazia 125 a distinctly more upmarket and aspirational character compared to the functional Activa family. 
 - Under-seat storage, a 5.3-litre fuel tank with approximately 55 to 60 kmpl claimed efficiency and a comfortable 780 mm seat height make the Grazia practical for daily urban commuting while the premium visual quality and technology presentation position it clearly above standard utility scooters. 
 - Available in Matte Axis Grey Metallic, Pearl Igneous Black, Rebel Red Metallic and Pearl Dusk Yellow, the Grazia 125 is priced at approximately Rs 82,000 to Rs 89,000 ex-showroom competing with Yamaha Fascino 125 Fi, Suzuki Access 125 and TVS Jupiter 125 where Honda's build quality and premium feature list at a competitive price are the key purchase drivers.
competitor_vehicles: Yamaha Fascino 125, TVS Jupiter 125, Suzuki Access 125

remarks: Large-wheel comfort scooter preferred by older riders and women
feature_summary:
The Honda Aviator is a larger, comfort-focused 110cc automatic scooter powered by a 109.2cc air-cooled, 4-stroke carburetted engine producing approximately 8 PS, designed with a larger, more upright unisex scooter format that prioritises comfort, generous storage and everyday practicality over sporty styling, appealing to mature buyers and family users seeking a more relaxed urban two-wheeler. 
 - The Aviator features a larger body compared to the standard Activa, with approximately 22 litres of under-seat storage, a wider and more cushioned seat for enhanced comfort on longer urban journeys, a large front apron compartment and Honda's ACG silent starter for vibration-free quiet engine ignition. 
 - Telescopic front suspension and twin rear shock absorbers deliver a plush and comfortable ride experience, while a front disc brake with CBS and rear drum with CBS on select variants provide safe stopping, and 12-inch alloy wheels with tubeless tyres ensure puncture resistance and stable urban handling. 
 - Chrome accents, dual-tone colour options, a wider body stance and a distinctive large-body scooter design give the Aviator an appeal among mature buyers and couples who want more comfortable and practical scooter transportation compared to the more nimble and compact Activa platform. 
 - Available in Honda's standard quality colour palette, the Aviator has gradually been transitioned out of the active primary lineup in favour of the more modern Activa 125 and updated scooters, but continues to attract buyers in the pre-owned market given its comfort, storage capacity and Honda reliability reputation. 
 - Originally priced at approximately Rs 68,000 to Rs 73,000 ex-showroom, competing with Suzuki Burgman Street and TVS Wego in the larger-body comfort scooter category where Honda's ACG silent start, generous storage and brand quality are the primary ownership benefits valued by its core buyer demographic.
competitor_vehicles: TVS Jupiter, Hero Maestro Edge 125, Suzuki Access 125

remarks: Ultra-budget entry-level scooter for price-sensitive buyers
feature_summary:
The Honda Cliq is Honda's ultra-lightweight, entry-level 110cc automatic scooter powered by a 109cc air-cooled, 4-stroke, 2-valve OHC single-cylinder fuel-injected engine, designed with a focus on minimalism, low weight of approximately 99 kg, compact dimensions and the lowest accessible price point, targeting first-time scooter buyers, older riders and urban users needing a simple, reliable short-range urban runabout. 
 - The defining features of the Cliq include small 10-inch alloy wheels, a unique underseat cargo hook for hanging bags or shopping, Honda's PGM-FI fuel injection as standard despite entry-level pricing, and a compact lightweight body making it the easiest Honda scooter to manoeuvre, park and handle in tight urban spaces. 
 - Conventional leading link front fork and twin rear shock absorbers provide adequate ride comfort, a front drum brake with CBS and rear drum brake manage stopping performance safely, and the low 760 mm seat height ensures accessibility for shorter and older riders who might struggle with taller and heavier standard scooters. 
 - The analogue instrument cluster, a small 3.5-litre fuel tank and compact overall dimensions make the Cliq ideally suited for very short-range urban trips and local errands where ease of use and simplicity are more important than touring range or advanced features. 
 - Available in Matte Axis Grey Metallic and Pearl Igneous Black, the Cliq is Honda's most niche urban mobility product, positioned primarily for customers who want the lightest, most manageable and most affordable Honda-quality scooter available in the market. 
 - Priced at approximately Rs 67,000 to Rs 72,000 ex-showroom, the Cliq competes with lightweight city-focused scooters from TVS and Hero where its Honda brand trust, PGM-FI injection reliability and minimal weight and complexity are the defining purchase factors for its niche but loyal buyer base.
competitor_vehicles: TVS Scooty Pep+, Hero Pleasure+, Yamaha Fascino

vehicle_model_aliases: Honda e:1, Activa Electric, Honda Activa EV
major_changes: Honda's first electric scooter for India under the Activa brand
remarks: Honda's entry into India's electric scooter market; swappable battery ecosystem
feature_summary:
The Honda Activa EV (e:1) is Honda's first mass-market electric scooter for India, built on a dedicated electric platform featuring a 1.8 kWh swappable Honda Mobile Power Pack e: battery system producing approximately 6 PS continuous power and 15 Nm of instant torque from a permanent magnet electric motor, designed around Honda's innovative swappable battery infrastructure. 
 - The Honda Mobile Power Pack (MMP e:) swappable battery system is the centrepiece of the e:1's design, allowing riders to exchange depleted battery packs for fully-charged ones at Honda Power Pack Exchanger e: swap stations in minutes rather than waiting hours for a conventional plug-in charge — directly addressing India's most significant EV adoption barrier around charging time and home charging infrastructure. 
 - Smart connectivity features include a fully digital instrument console with Bluetooth smartphone connectivity, battery charge level indicator, range estimation, mode selection display and compatibility with Honda's Road Sync Duo app for navigation, trip data and vehicle status monitoring, delivering a connected EV experience. 
 - Two riding modes — Standard and ECON — manage power delivery for maximum range or balanced everyday performance, while a regenerative braking system recovers kinetic energy during deceleration to extend the effective range per charge cycle, similar to Honda's global electric vehicle engineering philosophy. 
 - A 12-inch front and 10-inch rear wheel setup, telescopic front forks and twin rear shock absorbers, front disc with CBS and rear drum braking, and the low-speed instant torque character of the electric motor ensure a practical and manageable urban riding experience for the e:1's target city commuter buyer profile. 
 - Priced at approximately Rs 1.00 lakh to Rs 1.10 lakh ex-showroom with FAME-II subsidies applied, the Honda e:1 competes with Ola S1 Air, TVS iQube S and Ather 450S where Honda's brand trust and the innovative swappable battery ecosystem are its primary differentiators against rivals with larger conventional fixed battery packs.
competitor_vehicles: Ola S1 Air, TVS iQube, Bajaj Chetak, Ather 450S

facelift_description: Multiple updates over generations before discontinuation
major_changes: Replaced by Dio 125 under BS6 transition in 2021
remarks: Original 110cc Dio replaced by 125cc version post BS6 norms
feature_summary:
The Honda Dio 110 is the original sporty 110cc entry-level scooter that established Honda's youth-focused scooter category in India, powered by a 109.2cc air-cooled, 4-stroke, 2-valve OHC single-cylinder engine producing approximately 8 PS and 8.9 Nm, with CVT automatic transmission, distinguished by an edgy and sporty design that significantly differentiated it from the conventional rounded Activa silhouette when it was first launched. 
 - The Dio 110 features Honda's ACG silent starter for smooth vibration-free ignition, conventional telescopic front suspension as an upgrade over leading-link units on base scooters, a spring-loaded rear shock absorber and 10-inch alloy wheels with tubeless tyres ensuring comfortable and reliable urban ride quality. 
 - An optional front disc brake with CBS and rear drum with CBS provides a safety advantage at this price point, while the low seat height, compact body and lightweight construction of approximately 107 kg make it easy to manoeuvre in the most congested city traffic conditions. 
 - The Dio 110's angular body panels, distinctive sporty headlamp design, compact tail section and agile 110cc stance successfully differentiated it from the mature-buyer Activa positioning, building a loyal following among young college-going riders and new entrants to the scooter category across India. 
 - Under-seat storage for a half-face helmet, a 5.3-litre fuel tank with approximately 55 to 60 kmpl claimed efficiency, sporty colour options including Pearl Igneous Black, Matte Axis Grey, Rebel Red and Nautical Blue, and Honda's ACG silent start technology together make the Dio 110 a practical and stylish urban scooter. 
 - Priced at approximately Rs 68,000 to Rs 75,000 ex-showroom, the Dio 110 competes with Yamaha Ray ZR 110, TVS Scooty Zest and Hero Destini 125 where Honda's brand reliability, sporty styling and ACG silent start continue to attract young first-time scooter buyers across India's urban and Tier 2 markets.
competitor_vehicles: TVS NTorq, Yamaha Ray ZR, Suzuki Let's

major_changes: Unique crossover concept between scooter and motorcycle
feature_summary:
The Honda Navi is a uniquely positioned crossover urban vehicle that blends the anatomy of a small motorcycle with the convenience of an automatic scooter, powered by a 109.19cc air-cooled, 4-stroke, 2-valve OHC fuel-injected engine producing approximately 7.9 PS and 9 Nm of torque, with CVT automatic transmission and a distinctive customisable mini-adventure bike styling unlike any other product in Honda's lineup. 
 - The Navi features 12-inch wheels — larger than typical 110cc scooters — with knobby-tread tyres front and rear giving it a rugged mini-adventure bike appearance and mild capability over uneven urban surfaces, while the full underbody panel, motorcycle-like handlebar, upright ergonomics and beak front fender complete the distinctive crossover character. 
 - Honda designed the Navi with a modular body kit approach at launch offering various customisation accessories and body panel options for personalisation, targeting young adventurous buyers who want something genuinely distinctive and customisable rather than a conventional utility scooter or a standard commuter motorcycle. 
 - Conventional telescopic front fork and rear twin shock absorbers offer adequate ride comfort and some rough-road capability, CBS braking with front drum and rear drum provides safe stopping performance, and a 3.8-litre fuel tank with approximately 50 to 55 kmpl efficiency makes it fuel-efficient for its intended urban short-range use profile. 
 - Available in vibrant colours including Sparkling Orange Yellow, Hurly Burly Red, Patriot Blue and Pearl Precious White, the lightweight 110 kg kerb weight, 765 mm seat height and agile dimensions make the Navi one of Honda's most creative and experimental products in the Indian market. 
 - Priced at approximately Rs 72,000 to Rs 78,000 ex-showroom, the Honda Navi occupies a unique niche with very few direct competitors, appealing to buyers who want to stand out with a genuinely different two-wheeler that combines Honda's fuel-injected reliability with mini-adventure bike aesthetics and urban scooter convenience.
competitor_vehicles: TVS Scooty Pep+, Hero Pleasure+, Yamaha Fascino

major_changes: Lighter, sportier version of Activa with smaller wheels
remarks: Discontinued; replaced by Activa 6G and Dio 125 positioning
feature_summary:
The Honda Activa i is a lightweight, entry-level variant of the Activa family powered by a 109.19cc air-cooled, 4-stroke, 2-valve OHC single-cylinder engine updated to fuel injection in BS6 compliance, producing approximately 8 PS and 9 Nm, designed as a more affordable and simpler alternative to the main Activa lineup for budget-conscious buyers in Tier 2, Tier 3 and rural markets. 
 - The Activa i uses leading link front suspension rather than telescopic forks reflecting its entry-level cost positioning, paired with twin rear shock absorbers for adequate ride comfort, while later versions incorporated Honda's ACG silent starter providing the smooth, quiet ignition experience associated with Honda's broader premium scooter range. 
 - A front drum brake with CBS and rear drum brake provide the braking system, while 12-inch alloy wheels with tubeless tyres on updated versions ensure puncture resistance and stable handling, with an analogue speedometer and digital fuel gauge instrument cluster providing essential ride information in a no-frills format. 
 - Under-seat storage accommodating a half-face helmet, a 5.3-litre fuel tank with approximately 55 to 60 kmpl claimed efficiency and a low accessible seat height make the Activa i practical and economical for short urban commuting with a lightweight and easy-to-manoeuvre character. 
 - Available in Matte Axis Grey Metallic, Pearl Igneous Black and Rebel Red, the Activa i targets price-sensitive buyers in Tier 2 and Tier 3 cities and rural markets where the Honda brand's reliability, service network accessibility and strong resale value give it a meaningful advantage over lesser-known budget scooter brands. 
 - Priced at approximately Rs 65,000 to Rs 72,000 ex-showroom, the Activa i represents the most accessible entry point into the Honda Activa family, competing with Hero Pleasure Plus and TVS Scooty Zest where Honda brand trust, ACG silent start on updated variants and superior long-term reliability are the decisive purchase factors for budget-conscious first-time scooter buyers.
competitor_vehicles: TVS Jupiter, Hero Maestro, Yamaha Fascino

major_changes: Successive generation updates to engine, body, features before BS6
remarks: Legacy Activa generations replaced by Activa 6G with BS6 compliance
feature_summary:
The Honda Activa 3G, 4G and 5G represent three successive generations of India's best-selling scooter that defined and refined the Activa formula across different technology eras, all powered by variants of the core 109cc air-cooled, 4-stroke engine progressing from carburettor through improved carburettor to fuel injection, producing 8 to 8.5 PS and 8.5 to 9 Nm, establishing the Activa name as synonymous with scooter reliability in Indian consumer consciousness. 
 - The Activa 3G introduced a more powerful engine, a stylish new body design with external rear-view mirrors, an external fuel filler cap, a mobile charging socket and a new instrument cluster as meaningful upgrades over the 2G, while the 4G added Honda's Combi-Braking System with Equalizer technology and an updated colour palette targeting the aspirational commuter segment. 
 - The Activa 5G introduced Honda's ACG silent starter technology as a first for the Activa family — eliminating the loud starter motor noise and providing whisper-quiet vibration-free ignition — alongside an updated design with a new face, an LED tail lamp, a maintenance-free battery and a refined colour palette as important quality of life improvements. 
 - All three generations share the core Activa formula of CVT automatic transmission, 12-inch alloy wheels with tubeless tyres, a flat floorboard for easy boarding, under-seat storage of approximately 18 to 21 litres, a 5.3-litre fuel tank, an upright comfortable riding position and Honda's legendary build reliability that defined scooter ownership standards. 
 - These three Activa generations collectively drove Honda's market leadership in Indian scooters through the 2013 to 2020 period, establishing the Activa as India's number one two-wheeler by sales volume for multiple consecutive years and setting the benchmark against which all rival 110cc scooters were measured. 
 - These generations remain extremely popular in the pre-owned market where Honda's engine longevity, wide service network, affordable spare parts availability and consistently strong resale values make them excellent value second-hand purchases even after several years of ownership, reflecting the enduring quality of the Honda Activa platform.
competitor_vehicles: TVS Jupiter, Hero Destini 125, Suzuki Access 125

major_changes: Premium maxi-scooter launched as CBU import in India
remarks: Premium 160cc maxi-scooter, CBU import targeting premium urban riders
feature_summary:
The Honda PCX160 is a premium maxi-scooter powered by a 156.9cc liquid-cooled, fuel-injected, 4-stroke, 4-valve SOHC single-cylinder engine with Honda's eSP+ technology producing 15.8 PS at 8,500 rpm and 15.3 Nm at 6,500 rpm, paired with a CVT automatic transmission, positioning itself as Honda's most sophisticated and premium automatic scooter in the sub-200cc segment with international quality and executive styling. 
 - The PCX160 uses a steel underbone frame with 31 mm telescopic front forks and twin rear shock absorbers, a 220 mm front disc and 130 mm rear drum with Honda's combined ABS system, 14-inch front and 13-inch rear alloy wheels with 100/80-14 front and 120/70-13 rear tubeless tyres for composed and confidence-inspiring handling on both city roads and highways. 
 - Honda Smart Key system with keyless ignition, answer-back and security alarm functions, a 5-inch TFT colour digital instrument display with Bluetooth Honda RoadSync connectivity for smartphone integration, turn-by-turn navigation, call alerts, a 12V USB-C power outlet and a 12V accessory socket make the PCX160 the most technologically equipped Honda scooter in the 150cc-plus class. 
 - The PCX160's exceptional 30-litre under-seat storage — among the largest in any 150cc-plus scooter — accommodates a full-face helmet with room to spare, while additional front storage, liquid-cooled engine refinement, a keyless smart key system and combined ABS contribute to its appeal as a premium executive urban commuter. 
 - The liquid-cooled engine delivers approximately 45 to 50 kmpl efficiency with an 8-litre fuel tank for a practical urban range, with the CVT and liquid cooling providing a refined, quiet and premium ride quality significantly superior to air-cooled scooters at similar price points. 
 - Available in Pearl Glare White, Mat Gunpowder Black Metallic and Matte Axis Grey Metallic, the PCX160 is priced at approximately Rs 1.40 lakh to Rs 1.55 lakh ex-showroom, competing with Yamaha Aerox 155 and Aprilia SR 160 where Honda's liquid-cooled refinement, Smart Key technology, 30-litre storage and TFT Bluetooth connectivity make it the definitive premium executive maxi-scooter choice in India.
competitor_vehicles: Yamaha Aerox 155, Aprilia SR 160, TVS NTorq 125 Race Edition
